A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 17-page versions of the same G2PM study despite the changed title. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–B without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original G2PM benchmark results in Tables 2–6, design ablations in Table 1 and Figure 5, and model/data scaling experiments in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark, ablation, scaling, and cross-domain experimental results reported for G2PM.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same random-walk tokenizer, Transformer encoder/decoder, EMA reconstruction targets, masked-substructure objective, augmentations, and downstream prediction procedure.

E1.justification: The datasets and node classification, link prediction, graph classification, and cross-domain tasks are unchanged. The revised contribution bullet does not introduce coverage: Cora, Pubmed, and ogbl-Collab link prediction already appears in v2 Table 3.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2–6 and the scaling and heterophily comparisons. In particular, Table 3 retains GCN and GraphMAE as the link-prediction baselines.

E3.justification: Sections 3–5 and Appendix B retain the same splits, metrics, linear-probing and fine-tuning procedures, model configurations, and training budgets. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Table 1 and Figure 5 retain the same architecture, tokenization, augmentation, reconstruction, EMA, and masking ablations. Scaling, convergence, receptive-field, and cross-domain analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 states in both versions that experiments are conducted five times with different random seeds. The same ± reporting is retained, without new uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: All numerical tables and plotted results match. For example, Table 3 retains G2PM Hit@20 scores of 90.4 ± 0.8 on Cora and 88.0 ± 3.8 on Pubmed, and Hit@50 of 47.1 ± 0.6 on ogbl-Collab.

T1.justification: The graph and random-walk definitions and Equations (1)–(7) are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same conceptual account of substructure dependencies; no formal result, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The final introduction contribution explicitly extends its state-of-the-art claim from 'node and graph classification' to 'node/link/graph-level tasks.' This is a limited expansion of the summary claim: links were already covered in the abstract and Table 3, and other core claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of scaling, pretraining, augmentation, and transfer results are unchanged, as are Appendix A's mechanism explanations and the conclusion's discussion of ordered sequences and adaptive tokenizers. No substantive limitation or qualification is added.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same hardware/software information, optimizer, 100-epoch training, tuning ranges, and hyperparameter Tables 7–8. The abstract's code and dataset access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6, the citations, and the bibliography are unchanged. The positioning relative to GPM, graph Transformers, generative pretraining, and random-walk methods remains the same.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Scalable Graph Generative Modeling via Substructure Sequences' to 'Generative Graph Pattern Machine.' Section 2 drops 'Method:' from its heading, one contribution bullet is revised, and the version stamp and funding acknowledgment are updated. The remaining prose and organization match.

P2.justification: The replacement of the two-line title with a single-line title changes front-page spacing and shifts Figure 1 upward. Pages 3 and 10 have local text reflow. Figure/table designs, captions, axes, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision primarily retitles the paper, updates editorial details, and explicitly includes existing link-prediction work in the contribution summary. Methods, results, analyses, and appendix reproducibility information are unchanged. These limited edits do not materially alter the paper's clarity, evidential support, or overall quality.
